metadata.title: Boston, Clinton, Fitchburg and New Bedford Railroad (with predecessors and successors)
metadata.description: The BCF&NB system in Massachusetts: Fitchburg - Framingham - Mansfield - Taunton - New Bedford, Framingham - Lowell, the Marlborough, Sterling Junction, Attleboro and Fairhaven branches. Each line is split at every change of operator (Rule 4): Fitchburg and Worcester / Framingham and Lowell / New Bedford and Taunton, then Boston, Clinton and Fitchburg (1869-1876), the BCF&NB itself (1876-1879), the Old Colony (1879-1893) and the New York, New Haven and Hartford (1893-).
not_yet_sourced: Operator of the Agricultural Branch lines 1855-1869 (Framingham - Northborough - Marlborough) and of Northborough - Pratts Junction 1866-1869: passenger service is confirmed but the operator is not; those years are HELD, not drawn.
Mansfield and Framingham 1870-1873 operator: BC&F "immediately" (WFOX) vs BC&F lease from 1 Jan 1873 (WAB, WFRS). Drawn as BC&F from 1870.
Lease of the New Bedford Railroad to the BC&F: 2 Feb 1874 (WAB, WNBR) vs 1875 (WNBT, WTB); NCS may mean the NBRR itself ran trains 1874-1876. Drawn as BC&F 1874-1876.
Taunton Branch / New Bedford and Taunton 1840-1874: drawn as one NB&T operation; whether one or two companies should be named is open.
Exact day of the 1879 Old Colony lease and its term (99 vs 999 years).

[OPEN] ends: Pratts Jct - Sterling Jct (last confirmed 1920), Framingham - Lowell (last confirmed 1932), Mansfield - Taunton (last confirmed 1951), Attleboro Branch (last confirmed 1920), Fairhaven Branch (last confirmed 1932). [OPEN] start: Attleboro Branch (first confirmed 1876). [ANCHOR]: Fairhaven Branch 1876 for the BCF&NB.
Sterling Centre - Sterling Junction: WAB says the track was lifted after 1898; Fowler lists passenger stops there in 1904 and 1920. Unresolved.
Framingham - Fitchburg end 1931 and Framingham - Marlborough end 1937 rest on one secondary source (Humphrey & Clark via WFRM).
All headways and speeds are estimates.
omitted: Agricultural Branch 1855-1869 and Northborough - Pratts Jct 1866-1869: operator unknown (held).
Mansfield - Taunton 1836-1840: Boston and Providence operation, drawn in that layer.
Attleboro Branch 1871-1876 and Fairhaven Branch before 1876: passenger use not attested.
Middleborough and Taunton (Weir Jct - Middleborough): never a BCF&NB line.
Walpole - Foxboro event/commuter service 1971- and MBTA South Coast Rail 2025-: other operators, in the MBTA layer.
Lancaster Mills, Framingham Prison, Acushnet and Weir branches: freight only (Rule 1).
metadata.freight_only_audit: No freight-only years drawn: every line ends at its passenger end (freight afterlives are mentioned in notes only).
metadata.horsecar_audit: None: all constituent lines were steam roads from opening.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap with opstrace.py. Drawn 9.2 mi against 9.8 mi documented (Fowler line 72: South Framingham 21.4 - Marlborough Jct 29.8 = 8.4 mi, plus the 1.4-mi Marlborough branch; -6%). Fully traced, no straight-line leg: South Framingham - Framingham Centre - Marlborough Jct on the surviving CSX Fitchburg Secondary (tagged old_railway_operator=NYNH&H), Marlborough Jct - Marlborough on an untagged abandoned grade. The Marlborough end stops where the mapped grade ends, about 0.5 mi short of the documented branch length; the Marlborough depot site is not drawn. South Framingham - Framingham Centre is the 1855 realigned line, which is correct for every era drawn here (the 1849 Boston and Worcester alignment along Franklin St is not used). Framingham Centre waypoint hand-pinned (Nominatim returned the Massachusetts Turnpike).

segments.note: Boston, Clinton and Fitchburg operation of the Agricultural Branch main line (South Framingham - Framingham Centre - Marlborough Junction) and its Marlborough branch; the Agricultural Branch Railroad was renamed the BC&F in 1867 and the BC&F's own rail operations date from 1869 (NCS). Passenger trains ran on this line from 1855 (WAB), but who ran them before 1869 is not established: Nashua City Station (from the ICC valuation) gives the Agricultural Branch company no rail operations and dates the BC&F's from 1869, so 1855-1869 is held, not drawn. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

segments.note: New Haven operation. Through cars to Boston ran until 1919, when Agricultural Branch trains were cut to Framingham (WFRM citing Humphrey & Clark). After the Northborough - Fitchburg service was cut back in 1931 this was the route of the Framingham - Marlborough trains; the NYNH&H discontinued passenger service into Marlborough in 1937 (WAB; WFRM citing Humphrey & Clark: "cut back to Marlborough in 1931, and passenger service ended in 1937"). Approximate year from one secondary source; Fowler shows Fayville, Southboro and Marlboro Jct present in 1932, consistent. Freight continued (Marlborough branch abandoned 1966; Framingham - Marlborough Jct is today's CSX Fitchburg Secondary) - not drawn. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

properties.geometry_quality: Traced from OpenStreetMap with opstrace.py. Drawn 28.8 mi against 28.9 mi documented (Fowler line 72: Marlborough Jct 29.8 - Fitchburg 58.7). Marlborough Jct - Northborough - Clinton - Pratts Jct - Leominster on the surviving CSX Fitchburg Secondary (tagged NYNH&H); Leominster - Fitchburg, abandoned, on the Twin Cities Rail Trail (an untagged cycleway on the grade, 3.8 mi) and NYNH&H-tagged abandoned ways into Fitchburg. One approximated STRAIGHT LINE of 0.2 mi at Leominster, where the mapped trail begins beyond the end of the CSX track. The Fitchburg end stops where the mapped grade ends, about 0.1 mi short of the Fitchburg station site. Drawn on the surviving alignment throughout; no realignment is recorded, but the 1850/1866 alignments are assumed, not verified, to be the same.

segments.note: Boston, Clinton and Fitchburg operation, Marlborough Junction - Northborough (Agricultural Branch main line, 1855) - Berlin - Clinton - Pratts Junction (BC&F extension, opened July 1866, WAB) - Leominster - Fitchburg (Fitchburg and Worcester, merged into the BC&F 30 June 1869). The BC&F's rail operations date from 1869 (NCS). Passenger trains ran Marlborough Jct - Northborough from 1855 and on to Pratts Junction from 1866, but the operator before 1869 is not established, so those years are held, not drawn; Pratts Jct - Fitchburg 1850-1869 is drawn as the Fitchburg and Worcester. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

segments.note: Fitchburg and Worcester Railroad, opened 11 February 1850, "18 miles from Fitchburg through Leominster and Sterling to Sterling Junction" (WFW), where it met the Worcester and Nashua for Worcester. Nashua City Station (from the ICC valuation) gives the F&W rail operations 1850-1869, with no lease to another company recorded. Ends 1869, merger into the Boston, Clinton and Fitchburg (30 June 1869); service continued under the BC&F. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

Nashua City Station gives the M&F itself no rail operations, which supports another company running it from 1870; the 1875 merger into the BC&F is not a change of operator. If the 1873 lease date is right, 1870-1873 has an unnamed operator. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

Fully traced on the NYNH&H-tagged Massachusetts Coastal Middleboro Subdivision, Attleboro - Chartley - Barrowsville - Norton Furnace, no straight-line leg; it ends at Whittenton Junction (Taunton) and its last 0.8 mi shares track with the Mansfield - Taunton line. Built 1871; drawn on the surviving alignment.

segments.note: Old Colony operation under its lease of the BCF&NB (1879; the BCF&NB was consolidated into the Old Colony 5 March 1883, a paper change, not a change of operator). Old Colony leased to the New York, New Haven and Hartford from 1 March 1893. The Old Colony's 1889 timetable names the branch "Attleboro to Whittenton Junction" (NCS route list). Headway is an estimate, not sourced.

segments.note: Boston, Clinton, Fitchburg and New Bedford formed 1 June 1876 by consolidating the Boston, Clinton and Fitchburg with the New Bedford Railroad (WBCF; Nashua City Station gives 31 May 1876). 1879 is the Old Colony lease: BCF&NB stockholders had sanctioned it by 7 Feb 1879 (Springfield Weekly Republican); the takeover day is not established, so the split is by year only. ANCHOR: the only in-era passenger evidence is the 1876 Pathfinder (Fowler "y" at Fairhaven, Mattapoisett and Marion). Service certainly ran wider both ways, but no other year is confirmed for this operator; drawn to the 1879 lease as the report's drawable span directs. MEDIUM-LOW CONFIDENCE on the operator: the Fairhaven Branch Railroad (1854) was conveyed to the New Bedford and Taunton on 1 July 1861 (NCS, WFH), so it passed to the New Bedford Railroad and the BC&F lease by inheritance, but no source says in so many words that the BCF&NB ran trains on it. Pre-1876 service (WFH: opened 1854, uncited) is omitted until a source dates it and names the operator. Headway is an estimate, not sourced.
